image_description: A low-resolution image showing the dorsal side of a large marine mammal, likely a whale, surfacing in choppy green-grey water. The visible portion includes the arched back and head area, featuring mottled dark grey skin with distinct white patches (likely barnacles or cyamids). No dorsal fin is visible, consistent with a grey whale. The horizon line is visible in the background under a hazy sky.

checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The angle of the photo and the water level obscure the top of the head; blowholes are not clearly visible due to resolution and splash.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Skin is mottled grey to greyish-black with distinctive white patches from barnacles and whale lice.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The visible skin clearly shows the characteristic mottled grey pattern with irregular white patches typical of grey whale callosities/barnacles.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: No dorsal fin present; multiple dorsal knuckles along posterior back.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: There is no triangular dorsal fin. Instead, a series of small humps (knuckles) can be faintly discerned along the ridge of the back leading away from the viewer.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Robust spindle-shaped body of enormous proportions.

checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The mouth is submerged; baleen plates are internal/ventral structures not visible in this dorsal view.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Flippers (pectoral fins) are broad and paddle-shaped, remarkably elongated relative to body size.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: Pectoral fins are located ventrally/laterally and are submerged or out of frame.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Tail flukes are broad with smooth trailing edge and central notch.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The tail is completely submerged or out of the frame.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Skin texture is rough with callosities.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: Despite low resolution, the surface appears uneven and textured rather than smooth, consistent with rough skin/callosities.

The water texture appears slightly repetitive and 'smudged' in the foreground, lacking the crisp specular highlights expected in a high-quality photograph, though this may also be due to compression.
